Trump called the mayor of Chicago "useless" after his visit to Pope Leo XIV

US President Donald Trump again argued in absentia with Pope Leo XIV. A few hours after the prayer for peace, which was led by the pontiff, Trump wrote in Truth Social: "Someone should explain to the Pope that the Mayor of Chicago is useless, and that Iran cannot have a Nuclear Weapon!"

This was his reaction, among other things, to the visit of Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson to the Vatican. At the same time, as during the previous criticism of the pope on April 12, Trump did not directly respond to the words of Leo XIV.

The pope, in a prayer for peace, stated that peace cannot be a "naive illusion or a matter that can be managed for personal gain."

Israel has asked the United States to authorize expanded strikes on Beirut, according to sources cited by the Jerusalem Post. The request comes as the IDF announced Sunday that it had taken control of the Beaufort Ridge outpost and the Wadi al-Saluki areas north of the Litani River in southern Lebanon - territory that sits beyond the ceasefire line established under the November 2024 agreement.

The timing is notable. Israeli ground operations north of the Litani have been a persistent source of friction with both Washington and UNIFIL, and any U.S. green light for broader Beirut strikes would mark a significant shift in the administration's posture toward the Lebanese front - particularly while Gaza negotiations remain unresolved.

No U.S. response to the request has been reported yet.
